questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding liquidity trap?

i. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely inelastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

ii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly inelastic.

iii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

iv. It is the point where speculative demand for money and the liquidity preference curves are not related.

options.text: Only Statements i and ii are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement iii is correct.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A liquidity trap is a situation where monetary policy becomes ineffective due to the zero lower bound on interest rates.**
 
• **​**Liquidity trap:
 
• A liquidity trap refers to a situation in which an increase in the money supply does not result in a fall in the interest rate but merely in addition to idle balances the interest elasticity of demand for money becomes infinite.
 
• Under normal conditions, an increase in money supply, resulting in excess cash balances, would cause an increase in bond prices, as individuals sought to acquire assets in exchange for money, and a corresponding fall in interest rates.
 
• The horizontal portion of the liquidity preference curve is referred to as the liquidity trap.
 
• In this portion of the curve, the demand for money is infinitely elastic with respect to the interest rate.
 
• Re­ductions in the interest rate, in this portion only, increase people’s desire to hold cash balances
 
• Statement 3 is correct as It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.
 
• In a liquidity trap, people prefer holding money regardless of the interest rate because they expect that the return on other assets will not be better. Therefore, the demand for money is infinitely elastic (it does not change with interest rates), and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly horizontal or elastic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__"**

 
• 
 
Speculative Demand for Money: In a liquidity trap, speculative demand for money is actually infinitely elastic, not inelastic. This means that people are willing to hold an unlimited amount of money at a particular low interest rate, because they expect interest rates to rise in the future, which would cause bond prices to fall.

 
 
• 
 
Liquidity Preference Curve: The curve becomes perfectly elastic (horizontal) at the liquidity trap, indicating that changes in the money supply will not affect interest rates because people prefer to hold money rather than invest in bonds.

 Thus, this statement is incorrect because it incorrectly describes speculative demand for money as infinitely inelastic

questions.question: Proportional taxes would help to reduce the autonomous expenditure multiplier because ______.

options.text: MPC does not have any role in it

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**taxes reduce the MPC.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Proportional taxes:-**

 
 
• A proportional tax is one where everyone pays the same percentage of their income in taxes. This means that as income increases, so does the amount of tax paid.
 
• It would help to reduce the autonomous expenditure multiplier because taxes reduce the MPC.
 
• The MPC, or marginal propensity to consume, is the fraction of additional income that a person or household spends. When taxes increase, disposable income decreases, which in turn reduces the MPC.
 
• By reducing the MPC, proportional taxes can help to stabilize the economy by dampening the effects of fluctuations in autonomous expenditure, such as changes in investment or government spending.
 
• Other types of taxes, such as regressive taxes (where lower-income people pay a higher percentage of their income in taxes) or progressive taxes (where higher-income people pay a higher percentage of their income in taxes), could have different effects on the MPC and the autonomous expenditure multiplier.

questions.question: All of the following reasons can be attributed to the lack of access to credit for the poor EXCEPT:

options.text: lack of stable source of income
lenders prefer dealing in large loans in small numbers to minimise administration costs
absence of collateral with clear title

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**low information monitoring costs.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Lack of access to credit for the poor:-**

 
 
• It is a pervasive problem in many developing countries, and it can be attributed to various factors.
 
 
 
• One of the main reasons is the lack of a stable source of income, which makes it difficult for lenders to assess the creditworthiness of the borrower and increases the risk of default.
 
• Another reason is the absence of collateral with clear title, which makes it difficult for lenders to secure their loans and reduces their willingness to lend to poor borrowers.
 
• Lenders may also prefer dealing in large loans in small numbers to minimize administration costs, which can make it difficult for poor borrowers who need small loans to access credit.
 
• However, low information monitoring costs are not a reason for the lack of access to credit for the poor. In fact, low monitoring costs can make it easier for lenders to monitor the use of the loan and reduce the risk of default.

questions.question: Which among the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Industrial Securities Market is also known as gilt-edged market.
The secondary market is the market for the sale and purchase of previously issued securities.
RBI plays a dominant role in the gilt-edged market through its ‘Open Market Operations’.
The primary market is also known as new issue market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 1.**__** **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **No, the Industrial Securities Market** is not commonly known as the** gilt-edged market.**
 
• **The gilt-edged market, also known as the gilt market,** refers to the market for government bonds in the **United Kingdom.** These bonds are considered to be low-risk investments because they are backed by the UK government and are therefore seen as** "gilt-edged" investments.**
 
• On the other hand, the Industrial Securities Market refers to the market where industrial securities are traded. These securities include stocks, shares, and other investment products issued by companies in the industrial sector. This market is also commonly known as the stock market or the equity market.
 
• While both the gilt-edged market and the industrial securities market are important parts of the financial system, they are distinct markets with different investment products and characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The secondary market is a financial market **where investors buy and sell securities that have already been issued by companies or other entities. In contrast to **the primary market, where securities are issued for the first time, the secondary market involves the trading of existing securities between investors.**

 
 
• The secondary market includes exchanges such as **the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the NASDAQ, as well as over-the-counter (OTC) markets where securities** are traded directly between buyers and sellers without a centralized exchange. In the secondary market, the price of a security is determined by supply and demand, and fluctuations in market conditions can affect the price of securities traded on the market.
 
 
 
• ** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** plays a dominant role in the **gilt-edged market through its open market operations (OMOs)**.
 
 
• In the gilt-edged market, government securities (G-secs) are traded, and these securities are issued by the government to raise funds.
 
• The **RBI **is responsible for managing the demand and supply of G-secs in the market. One of the primary tools that the RBI uses to manage the demand and supply of **G-secs is through OMOs**.**OMOs are the buying and selling of government securities in the open market by the RBI.** 
 
• When th**e RBI wants to inject liquidity into the market**, it buys G-secs from the market, and when it wants to absorb liquidity from the market, it sells G-secs in the market. This helps in regulating the** money supply in the economy and controlling inflation.**
 
 
 
• **The primary market**, also known as the **new issue market,** is where **new securities are issued and sold for the first time to investors**.
 
 
• Companies, governments, and other organizations raise capital in the primary market by selling securities, such as stocks or bonds, to investors. The primary market is distinct from the secondary market, where securities that have already been issued are bought and sold between investors.

questions.question: Which of the following is issued by commercial banks at a discount on face value?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Certificates of deposits**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Certificates of deposits** are issued by commercial banks at a discount on face value.
 
• They are a type of time deposit with a fixed maturity date and specified interest rate.
 
• Certificates of deposits are negotiable instruments, meaning they can be transferred from one party to another.
 
• They are often used by banks to raise funds from the market.
 
• The interest rate on certificates of deposits is generally higher than that on regular savings accounts, making them an attractive investment option for large investors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Promissory notes** are written promises to pay a certain amount of money at a future date but are not issued at a discount.
 
• **Commercial papers** are unsecured short-term debt instruments issued by corporations, not commercial banks.
 
• **Treasury bills** are short-term government securities issued at a discount but by the government, not commercial banks.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an approach for measuring unemployment in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monthly Status Approach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monthly Status Approach **is NOT an approach for **measuring unemployment** in India.
 
• **Methods/measures for assessing unemployment:**
 
 
• **Usual status unemployment: **This method estimates the number of individuals who remained unemployed for a significant portion of the year. It typically provides the lowest estimates of unemployment.
 
• **Current weekly status: **This measure evaluates unemployment based on a single week. An individual is classified as unemployed if they were unable to work for any duration during the survey week.
 
• **Current daily status: **Under this approach, individuals who were unable to secure employment on one or more days during the survey week are considered unemployed. The daily status method is often seen as a comprehensive measure of unemployment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The unemployment rate** is calculated by dividing the number of unemployed individuals by the total labour force.
 
• The labour force comprises both employed and unemployed individuals. Individuals who are neither employed nor actively seeking employment, such as students and those engaged in unpaid domestic work, are categorized as being out of the labour force.
 
• According to the International Labour Organisation (ILO), unemployment is defined as being without a job, being available to work, and actively searching for employment.

questions.question: How many digits does the MMID code of any commercial bank have?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **MMID code** of any commercial bank has** 7 digits.**
 
• MMID stands for **Mobile Money Identifier.**
 
• It is a unique** 7-digit code** assigned by banks to their customers for mobile banking transactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Every mobile banking account has a **distinct MMID** that the bank assigns to the user.
 
• There can only be **one MMID Code** associated with a bank account.
 
• To transfer money using this function, an MMID is required for both the** sender and the recipient.**
 
• To take advantage of this service, one must register for **mobile banking services **with your bank.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding microfinance?

options.text: Micro finance organizations (MFIs), are Banks that provide micro financial services.
Other than Banks, Micro finance organizations (MFIs) are organizations that provide micro financial services.
Micro finance has the provision of giving loans to micro, small and medium enterprises.
RBI is the regulatory body for micro finance institutions (MFIs).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micro finance organizations (MFIs), are Banks that provide micro financial services.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Microfinance:-**

 
 
• It is a financial service that provides small loans, savings, and other financial services to low-income individuals or small businesses who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs) are organizations that offer microfinance services. These organizations can be banks or non-banking institutions.**
 
• Microfinance is important in promoting financial inclusion and reducing poverty by providing access to credit and other financial services to those who are excluded from traditional banking services.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the regulatory body for MFIs in India.

questions.question: As per ’Basel III: A global regulatory framework for more resilient banks and banking systems’ released in December 2010, banks will be required to hold a capital conservation buffer of ______ of risk weighted assets (RWAs) in the form of common equity to withstand future periods of stress.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.5%.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Basel III** is a set of international banking regulations developed by the Bank for International Settlements in order to promote stability in the international financial system.
 
• The **Basel Committee** published the Basel III rules text in **December 2010.**
 
• It covers the worldwide regulatory criteria on bank capital adequacy and liquidity that were agreed upon by the Governors and Heads of Supervision and adopted by the** G20 Leaders** at their November summit in Seoul.
 
• To withstand future periods of stress, banks will be required to keep a capital conservation buffer of **2.5%**__ of risk-weighted assets (RWAs) in the form of common equity under Basel III.
 
• The results of the Committee's complete **quantitative impact research** were also released (QIS).
 
• **Nout Wellink** was the Chairman of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
 
• Basel Committee on Banking Supervision examines and proposes ways to reconfigure global banking regulations.
 
• The Committee estimated that Group 1 banks in aggregate would have had a shortfall of €577 billion at the end of 2009.
 
• The Basel III accord increased the minimum Basel III capital requirements for banks from 2% in Basel II to 4.5% of common equity, as a percentage of the bank’s risk-weighted assets.
 
• In order to be Basel compliant, there is additionally a 2.5% buffer capital requirement, bringing the total minimum requirement to 7%.
 
• When banks are in financial distress, they can use the buffer, but doing so can result in even more financial constraints when it comes to paying dividends.
